The From address must be on a 24 domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. 25 26 ## 2. Create a client 27 28 `src/lib/resend.ts`: 29 30 ```ts 31 import { Resend } from "resend"; 32 33 export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); 34 ``` 35 36 Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). 37 Never expose the API key to the browser. 38 39 ## 3. Send an email 40 41 ```ts 42 import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; 43 44 const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ 45 from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, 46 to: "user@example.com", 47 subject: "Welcome!", 48 html: "

", 49 text: "Thanks for signing up.", 50 }); 51 ``` 52 53 `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. 54 55 ## 4. Send with a React template 56 57 Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: 58 59 ```tsx 60 import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; 61 import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; 62 63 await resend.emails.send({ 64 from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, 65 to: "user@example.com", 66 subject: "Reset your password", 67 react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), 68 }); 69 ``` 70 71 The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX 72 works too. 73 74 ## 5. # Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard.

content.text:
I added a welcome email and a password reset email using Resend, and wired both into `src/lib/users.ts`. I haven't sent a real email. Lint passes. `tsc` reports one error, `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` in `src/app/layout.tsx`, which I didn't touch. I think it's missing generated Next types. I chose Resend because `docs/resend.md` in the repo already describes it.

- **Welcome email:** I added `createUser({ email, name })` to `users.ts`. It rejects duplicate emails, adds the user, sends the welcome email and returns the user.
- **Password reset:** `requestPasswordReset(email)` creates a one-hour token and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. It does nothing for unknown emails, so nobody can probe which addresses are registered.
- **Failed sends:** `emails.send` returns an error instead of throwing, so a failed send is logged and doesn't break signup or the reset request.
- **Files:** `src/lib/email.ts` has the sending code, `src/lib/resend.ts` creates the client, and `src/emails/` has the two React templates. I also installed the `resend` package.
- **Credentials:** `.env.example` holds placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`. `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.

**Not working end to end yet:**
- **No `/reset-password` page:** the emailed link leads nowhere until you build one.
- **Tokens are in memory:** only the token hash is stored, and it's lost on restart. Nothing verifies the token yet, because the app has no database or sessions.
- **Nothing calls the new functions:** no route or form calls `createUser` or `requestPasswordReset` yet.

To send real email, put a real Resend API key in `.env.local` and use a sender on a domain you've verified in Resend. Until then `onboarding@resend.dev` works for testing.
